topic: How do phase noise and outdated CSI from long round-trip times influence robust precoding design for link budget reliability?
consensus_response: Phase noise from the on-board LO contributes significantly to channel phase variations, independent of user mobility. Outdated CSI at the GW due to long RTTs leads to unpredictable system performance. Robust precoder designs must account for spatial correlation of phase noise by optimizing against worst-case received SINR under bounded uncertainty or using random models to describe CSI imperfections. This approach ensures that the system performs optimally even with imperfect CSI, mitigating the impact of phase noise on system performance and link budget reliability.
reference_context: Satellite communication systems are characterized by a long round-trip delay (RTD) and imperfect channel state information (CSI), which degrades the performance of precoded L-band mobile multibeam satellite systems. Robust beamforming has been proposed to counteract signal-to-interference-and-noise ratio (SINR) degradation caused by CSI estimation error.
